sourceSystems.name: FeatureProof Requirements
sourceSystems.purpose: Product expectations for a local-first feature testing and parity review tool.

capabilities.name: Open a local feature proof file
capabilities.businessOutcome: A tester can load a .fproof file from disk and review the project checklist.
acceptanceSignals: The user can enter a local file path.
The app loads valid feature-proof/v1 files.
The dashboard, checks, and run history reflect the opened file.
dataRequirements: A valid .fproof file on the local filesystem.

capabilities.name: Record a test run
capabilities.businessOutcome: A tester can capture current validation results without overwriting previous run history.
acceptanceSignals: The user can start a new run with tester, version, browser, and URL context.
The user can record statuses and notes for individual checks.
Completed runs do not receive additional results.
dataRequirements: A loaded .fproof file with at least one check.

capabilities.name: Preserve collaboration-friendly diffs
capabilities.businessOutcome: Saving run results creates focused file diffs that are easy to review in git or shared-drive workflows.
acceptanceSignals: Saving preserves existing schema metadata and check definitions.
Saving does not add omitted optional fields to existing checks.
The meaningful saved change is limited to run data.
dataRequirements: A .fproof file with existing check metadata and at least one new result to save.

sourceSystems.name: FeatureProof Packaging Workflow
sourceSystems.purpose: Manual distribution process for sharing the app with users who do not have .NET installed.

capabilities.name: Create a self-contained distribution artifact
capabilities.businessOutcome: A lead can create one shareable package that includes platform-specific app builds.
acceptanceSignals: The archive contains Windows, Linux, and macOS app folders.
The archive does not include sample .fproof files.
dataRequirements: .NET SDK and PowerShell are available on the packaging machine.

capabilities.name: Run the packaged app without repository samples
capabilities.businessOutcome: A team member can launch FeatureProof from the package and choose their own feature proof file.
acceptanceSignals: The packaged app starts without requiring a .NET install.
The UI prompts the user for a local .fproof path.
The repository dogfood sample is not auto-loaded from the package.
dataRequirements: A packaged build for the tester's operating system.

sourceSystems.name: FeatureProof README
sourceSystems.purpose: Repository documentation for users and agents.

capabilities.name: Explain agent context requirements
capabilities.businessOutcome: A user can provide enough repository context for an agent to generate useful .fproof drafts.
acceptanceSignals: The README lists the format docs, schemas, source definition sample, and dogfood sample as useful context.
The README provides prompt templates for .fproofdef.json and .fproof generation.
The README includes review guidance before using generated checks.
